latest_substantive_result.summary: Appended the U continuation's selected report and code/results. The source reports a passive Gaussian pump/sensor relocation with identical specified controlled records and opposite bath-number-current signs; an attainable model-conditional current interval; and conditional phase-code/causal-filter identities. For positive bath weights, a positive lower endpoint equals the ordinary conservative raw-current test, and an ordinary phase-switched receiver with equal resources can run the same decoder. Other constructions and comparisons remain population- or fixture-bounded. No measured trace, physical heat/cooling, practical advantage, novelty or priority is established.

next_decisive_step: For any physical claim, acquire a calibrated device or lawfully supplied trace with complete bath, energy, and readout-plane calibration; test code-synchronous/upstream noise with independent controls; and compare against ordinary phase-switched and reference receivers at matched information and total cost. Obtain independent audits of the analytic arguments separately.

limitations: The exact opposite-current no-go is scoped to the stated passive Gaussian OU model class, including an allowed independent colored sensor OU component with the plant drift; it is not universal across all instruments or noise models.

Current intervals require the stated known plant, metric, bath and occupation inputs. The finite-error sampling result assumes independent proper-Gaussian snapshots; it does not cover a continuous trace without a separate acquisition model.
Positive-weight lower-endpoint certification adds no decision beyond the ordinary calibrated raw-covariance test. Number current is not heat without a physically justified energy observable.

The phase-code identity requires a physical intervention and stated code-independence conditions. An ordinary phase-switched receiver with the same resources implements the same decoder; code-synchronous and upstream noise require independent acquisition controls.

The continuous-filter positive-lag counterexample is not a full-record indistinguishability result. The destructive-pair method assumes conditional closure and inherited controllability, and its precision/biological validity is unresolved.
Numerical comparisons are synthetic and descriptive; source replay checks do not certify mathematical correctness or scientific validity.
No measured numerical trace was acquired. Physical heat/cooling, wall power, pump efficiency, total energy, novelty, external review, historical priority and practical advantage remain UNKNOWN.
